correctness.rationale: Each selected nonempty interval is contained in the first selected inclusion-maximal support type along an increasing-endpoint antichain path. If c follows p, first-owned strict subordinate types are precisely those inside c and not inside p; selecting t locally with >=1 maximal-copy gives B_pc(t)=binom(H_pc+a_c,t)-binom(H_pc,t). Coverage gain g_pc depends only on previous maximal right endpoint. A max-plus weighted count DP with state (last maximal interval, chosen cardinality) therefore enumerates each labeled committee once and sums precisely score-tied counts. Empty-support labels contribute binomial multiplicity at terminalization. O(m³+m²k²+n+m²) rational/integer arithmetic and <=m-bit counts are credible; telescoping counting gives exact unbiased weighted-backtracking sampler. Inspected source verify.py. Independent structurally different path-counting code matched brute-force optimum and winner multiplicity on 500 seeded instances up to 9 labeled candidates with zero voter weights and empty supports, including illustrative score 9 and 7 winners. Finite samples cannot prove ideal uniformity; counting bijection does.

value.rationale: Fair random selection from tied committees needs exact counts, which decision/optimization algorithms do not supply, especially with nested duplicate supports and empty candidates. A polynomial exact counting and uniform reconstruction theorem for natural voter-interval elections provides a nontrivial algorithmic complement to known winner determination.

final_claim: Exact polynomial-time counting of all labeled optimal fixed-k committees for weighted voter-interval Chamberlin–Courant coverage, including duplicate/nested/empty candidate intervals, and exact uniform winning-committee sampling with fair random bits.
limitations: Voter-interval candidate approvals and nonnegative rational voter weights; approval-based coverage CC, not arbitrary Thiele, circular arcs, negative weights or arbitrary approval matrices.
